questions.question: Money multiplier uses which of the following monetary instruments for its calculation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cash reserve ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The money multiplier** is a formula used to determine **the maximum amount of money **that can be created by commercial banks through the process of deposit multiplication.
 
• Cash reserve ratio (CRR) is the percentage of deposits that commercial banks are required to keep with the central bank as a reserve. It is a monetary policy tool used by central banks to regulate the money supply in the economy.
 
• The money multiplier is calculated by dividing the total amount of deposits by the cash reserve ratio. This means that the higher the cash reserve ratio, the lower the money multiplier, and vice versa.
 
• The other options mentioned in the question are also monetary policy tools used by central banks to regulate the money supply in the economy. However, they are not directly used in the calculation of the money multiplier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bank rate is the rate at which the central bank lends money to commercial banks. It is used as a tool to regulate the cost of borrowing in the economy.
 
• Reverse repo rate is the rate at which the central bank borrows money from commercial banks. It is used to regulate the liquidity in the economy.
 
• Repo rate is the rate at which the central bank lends money to commercial banks against securities. It is used to regulate the money supply in the economy.

questions.question: What happened in Bengal, India, in 1770 that resulted in the death of one-third of the population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Famine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Bengal Famine of 1770 **was a catastrophic event that resulted in the death of approximately** one-third of the population of Bengal**, which was then a province of British India.
 
• The famine was caused by a combination of factors, including a severe drought that lasted for two years, a failure of the monsoon rains, and the policies of the British colonial government.
 
• The British had imposed high taxes on the local population, which led to widespread poverty and malnutrition. When the drought hit, food prices skyrocketed, and many people could not afford to buy food.
 
• As a result, thousands of people died of starvation, and many more were forced to sell their land and possessions in order to survive. The famine had a lasting impact on the region and its people, and it remains a tragic and controversial chapter in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Chemical explosion - There is no evidence of any chemical explosion occurring in Bengal in 1770. Therefore, this option is incorrect.
 
• Massacre - While there were incidents of violence and unrest during the famine, there was no organized massacre of the population. This option is also incorrect.
 
• Slavery - Slavery was abolished in British India in 1843, so it is unlikely that it was a factor in the Bengal Famine of 1770. This option is incorrect.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of Inflammable substances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inflammable substances** are those that can easily catch fire and burn rapidly.
 
• **LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) and petrol **are examples of inflammable substances as they are highly flammable and can ignite easily.
 
• **Glass** is not an inflammable substance as it does not catch fire or burn. It is a non-combustible material.
 
• Alcohol, on the other hand, is a flammable substance but not as highly inflammable as LPG or petrol. It can ignite easily but does not burn as rapidly as the other two substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• LPG: It is a mixture of propane and butane gases and is commonly used as a fuel for cooking and heating purposes. It is highly flammable and can cause explosions if not handled properly.
 
• Petrol: It is a highly flammable liquid fuel used in internal combustion engines. It can easily catch fire and cause explosions if not handled properly.
 
• Glass: It is a transparent, hard, and brittle material that is made by cooling a molten mixture of silica, soda, and lime. It is widely used in the construction industry for windows, doors, and walls.
 
• Alcohol: It is a colorless, volatile liquid that is used as a solvent, fuel, and in the production of beverages. It is highly flammable and can easily ignite but does not burn as rapidly as other inflammable substances.

questions.question: A Money Bill should be returned to the Lok Sabha within ______ days by Rajya Sabha, either with recommendations or without recommendations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **As per Article 109 of the Indian Constitution**, if a **Money Bill **is passed by Lok Sabha and transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations, Rajya Sabha must return the Bill to Lok Sabha within 14 days from the date of receipt of the Bill.
 
• If Rajya Sabha fails to return the Bill within this period, the Bill is deemed to have been passed by both the Houses.
 
• If Rajya Sabha wants to make any recommendations to the Money Bill, it can do so within the 14-day period.
 
• Such recommendations may either be accepted or rejected by Lok Sabha. However, if Rajya Sabha fails to return the Bill within 14 days and the Bill is deemed to have been passed, it cannot make any recommendations to the Bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A Money Bill is a type of financial legislation that can only be introduced in Lok Sabha and not in Rajya Sabha. It deals with matters such as taxation, borrowing of money by the government, expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, etc.
 
• Unlike ordinary bills, Money Bills do not require the approval of Rajya Sabha. However, Rajya Sabha can make recommendations to the Bill, which Lok Sabha can either accept or reject.
 
• If there is a disagreement between the two Houses regarding a Money Bill, it is resolved by a joint sitting of both the Houses, where the Bill is passed by a simple majority of the total number of members of both the Houses.
 
• The Speaker of Lok Sabha is the final authority on the question of whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not. If there is any dispute regarding this, the Speaker's decision is final.

• Ranade believed that the remarriage of widows would not only provide them with a new lease of life but also help in the overall progress of society. He also advocated for the education of women and worked for their empowerment.
 
• Ranade's efforts bore fruit when the Widow Remarriage Act was passed in 1856, which legalized the remarriage of widows in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of “agro based industries"?

__
 
• **Iron and steel industry,** is NOT an example of "agro-based industries" because it does not involve the processing or manufacturing of agricultural products.
 
• Industries that rely on agricultural products derived from plants and animals are known as agro-based industries.
 
• Additionally, by processing and creating useful and marketable products, they increase the value of agricultural output.
 
• The textile, sugar, vegetable oil, tea, coffee, and leather goods sectors are a few instances of agro-based industries in India.

• Leather industry: This industry involves the processing of animal hides and skins into leather for various products such as shoes, bags, and furniture.

questions.question: Article 23-24 of the Indian Constitution deals with which of the following fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right against Exploitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 23-24 of the Indian Constitution **deals with **the Right against Exploitation**.
 
• This right is specifically aimed at preventing human trafficking, bonded labor, and other forms of forced labor.
 
• The right against exploitation also prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any hazardous work.
 
• In addition, this right also prohibits the sale and purchase of human beings, including women and children.
 
• Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution establish the right against exploitation.
 
• These crucial fundamental rights ensure that no individual is subjected to any form of forced labor. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options mentioned in the question are also fundamental rights enshrined in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Right to Equality ensures equal treatment before the law and prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• The Right to Freedom includes several sub-rights such as freedom of speech and expression, freedom of assembly, freedom of religion, and freedom of movement. The Right to Constitutional Remedies enables citizens to approach the courts to seek enforcement of their fundamental rights.

questions.question: The Almatti Dam of Karnataka is built over which of the following rivers?

• The Krishna River basin is the third-largest in India, covering an area of about 258,948 square kilometers.
 
• The river is an important source of irrigation, drinking water, and power generation for the states through which it flows.
 
• The Almatti Dam, also known as the Lal Bahadur Shastri Dam, is built across the Krishna River in the state of Karnataka. It is a multipurpose dam used for irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and flood control.
